Running in the Rain: 坚持晨跑的女孩与一次难忘的雨中训练。

Emma joined the school running team last autumn. Every morning at six thirty, she ran five kilometres around the lake with her teammates. In the beginning, she was often the last one, and her legs hurt for weeks.

Her coach, Mr Cross, told her, 'Don't compare yourself with others. Compare yourself with yesterday.' Emma wrote her daily time in a small notebook. Month after month, her time got better. In spring, she was no longer the last runner.

One morning in June, it started to rain heavily during the run. Other students stopped, but Emma kept running. The rain was cold, and her shoes were full of water, but she felt strong and free. When she crossed the finish line, her whole team was waiting and cheering for her.

Next month, Emma will run her first city race. She may not win a medal, but that doesn't matter to her any more. 'The girl who couldn't finish one kilometre has already won,' she wrote in her notebook that night.
